text:
Alex Ovechkin became the Capitals' all-time assists leader this week. It came in an otherwise rough stretch for him and for the team: 3 points in his last 10 games (4.8 expected), and five straight losses, all in regulation, by a combined 30-16.

How worried should you be? Less than the record suggests. Washington is 10-11-0 but has broken exactly even on expected goals for the season (the quality of chances) and has 53% at 5v5. Even during the skid it had 49%. The problem is in net: the Capitals have allowed about nine and a half more goals than their chances against would predict, and Charlie Lindgren is at .817 and 6.0 goals worse than expected over his last five starts (1-4-0). By our numbers they've earned two or three more points than they have, and our playoff odds still give them 33%.

The kids are the good news. Rookie defenceman Cole Hutson has emerged as one of the league's top rookie scorers, with a three-assist game last week, and Ryan Leonard scored in four straight. The Tom Wilson, Pierre-Luc Dubois and Aliaksei Protas line wins 60% of the expected goals at 5v5.

Jakob Chychrun's hit on Ottawa's Nick Cousins is still drawing headlines two weeks later. The top line of Alex Tuch, Dylan Strome and Jordan Kyrou has been outscored 7-5 despite winning 55% of the chances. What we'd watch: the crease.
